teaching.hint: Which two seats make the outcome final as soon as a displaced passenger chooses one?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Before either endpoint seat is selected, both passenger 1’s and passenger n’s seats remain equally available to every random chooser.
solution_outline.approach: Return 1 when n=1, otherwise one half. Explain the process as repeated random choices until either seat 1 or seat n is selected.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: While unresolved, both decisive seats are in the same set of available seats and have equal selection probability at each random step.
solution_outline.correctness: Choosing seat 1 ends displacement without harming passenger n; choosing seat n prevents their success. The two equally likely terminating events partition outcomes, so success probability is one half.
solution_outline.pitfall: Assuming the first passenger must directly choose seat 1 or seat n ignores displaced intermediate passengers.

common_wrong_turns: Treat an intermediate seat choice as a final failure
source_fidelity_notes: Made uniform random choice explicit and retained the one-passenger boundary case.
